answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a time-cost proof before a new identity gains full rights: each identity must accumulate a verifiable history of useful, rate-limited work over weeks, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs thousands of weeks of compute, not one script run. Like a whisper that only becomes trusted after it is repeated consistently, or an opal that gains value as it is cut and polished, reputation should accrue slowly and stay non-transferable. A comet-fast flood of fresh identities would then earn nothing, because rights follow proven history, not headcount.
